prompt: What does the lesson say monitoring an LLM application mostly is?

choices.text: Reading a sample of replies every hour
choices.why: That reads content; the lesson counts decisions.

choices.text: The existing defences, read as a stream
choices.why: Right: each verdict, counted over time.

choices.text: A second model judging the first one's replies
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson adds a model.

choices.text: Asking clients to rate every reply they get
choices.why: Reports are one signal among several.

prompt: Match each signal to what a jump in it usually means, according to the lesson's table.
hint: One meaning on the right belongs to no signal.

pairs.right: a prompt or model change broke the format
an agent proposing out of scope
a loop, before the ceiling stops everybody

prompt: Why does the lesson count decisions rather than storing the content of replies for the dashboard?

choices.text: Counts are cheap and hold no personal data
choices.why: Right: content stays in the log, under its retention.

choices.text: Content cannot be stored for more than a day
choices.why: Lesson 11 sets retention per tier; that is not the argument.

choices.text: Dashboards cannot display text
choices.why: They can; that is the danger.

choices.text: The model refuses to have its replies stored
choices.why: The model has no say in it.

prompt: How many calls did the assistant receive at 02:00 on the first day?
The lesson's warning about quiet hours: a rate computed over one call is a ___, not a measurement.
How many pages did the naive rule send in the 48 hours?
Why did the naive rule page at 03:00 and 04:00?
hint: Look at the counts on those lines.

choices.text: The night shift changed the prompt
choices.why: No change happened at night.

choices.text: The canary fired at night
choices.why: The canary fired at 14:00, and the naive rule does not watch it.

choices.text: The baseline was too low at night
choices.why: The naive rule has no baseline at all.

choices.text: One refusal out of one call is 100%
choices.why: Right: arithmetic, not an incident.

prompt: Which incidents did the naive rule miss? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: the canary in a reply at 14:00
choices.why: Yes: no rule watched the canary.

choices.text: the denied tool calls from 16:00
choices.why: Yes: no rule watched the gate.

choices.text: the refused replies from 10:00
choices.why: It caught those, among false pages.

choices.text: the client reports at 11:00
choices.why: Those were not an incident; one report an hour is ordinary.

prompt: What removed the night-time pages in the tuned rule for refused replies?

choices.text: A higher rate threshold, 5% instead of 2%
choices.why: One of one is still 100%.

choices.text: Ignoring every hour between midnight and six
choices.why: An incident at night would then be missed.

choices.text: A minimum of five events before it fires
choices.why: Right: one refusal in a quiet hour is under five.

choices.text: Comparing with the previous hour only
choices.why: It compares with the median of 24 hours.

prompt: Why does the canary rule have no baseline and no minimum?

choices.text: It should never happen, so one is enough
choices.why: Right: a baseline of zero makes "three times usual" meaningless.

choices.text: Canaries are too rare to compute a median
choices.why: Rarity is why one is enough, not a computing problem.

choices.text: Baselines only work for counts above a hundred
choices.why: The deny rule uses a baseline of 0.5.

choices.text: The canary rule is a ticket, not a page
choices.why: It is a page.

prompt: Why are refused replies a ticket and denied tool calls a page?

choices.text: Tickets are for counts below ten
choices.why: The refused replies counted ten and eleven.

choices.text: Pages are reserved for the provider's outages
choices.why: Two of the pages here are Tarefa's own signals.

choices.text: A broken format costs time; a pushed gate risks harm
choices.why: Right: severity follows what comes next.

choices.text: Refused replies happen only in working hours
choices.why: They happen at night too.

prompt: How many tickets did the tuned rules open?
What does the lesson say a quiet, healthy day and a dead monitoring job have in common?

choices.text: Both raise a ticket
choices.why: Neither raises anything; that is the problem.

choices.text: Both are caught by the canary rule
choices.why: The canary rule needs data to run on.

choices.text: Both reset the baselines
choices.why: Baselines are computed from the data present.

choices.text: Both look the same: nothing fires
choices.why: Right: which is why an hour with no data is an alert.

prompt: What does every alert carry, so that somebody half awake can act on it?

choices.text: The full text of the replies involved
choices.why: Content stays in the log; the alert carries numbers.

choices.text: A link to its runbook
choices.why: Right: what it means, where to look, what is safe to do.

choices.text: The phone number of the provider
choices.why: Most alerts are Tarefa's own to handle.

choices.text: A summary written by the model
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson has the model write alerts.

prompt: Which questions does the monthly review of the alert list ask? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Did every page need a person at that hour?
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Was every incident announced by a rule?
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Does every rule have a runbook and an owner?
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Can the thresholds be raised until nothing fires?
choices.why: That is how incidents go unannounced.

choices.text: Can the rules be edited in the dashboard to save time?
choices.why: The lesson keeps them in the repository, reviewed.

prompt: Put the steps from a control's verdict to a person's action in order.
hint: From one request to a runbook.
items: The decision is counted for the hour
A rule compares the count with its baseline
The alert reaches a person with its runbook

prompt: After a deployment, the count of canary hits drops from its usual zero to zero, and stays there. What does the lesson suggest checking?
hint: A count of zero after a change.

choices.text: Nothing, since zero is the healthy value
choices.why: Zero is also what a check that stopped running reports.

choices.text: That the baseline has been recomputed
choices.why: The canary rule has no baseline.

choices.text: That the model still writes system prompts
choices.why: The model never writes the system prompt.

choices.text: That the canary check is still in the path
choices.why: Right: a check that stopped running reports zero for ever.

prompt: Where does the lesson keep `alerts.json`, and why?

choices.text: In the repository, changed by a reviewed pull request
choices.why: Right: with the reason in its description.

choices.text: In the dashboard, so it changes fast
choices.why: Fast and unreviewed is the problem.

choices.text: On each on-call engineer's laptop
choices.why: Then nobody knows which version is running.

choices.text: In the call log, beside the replies
choices.why: The log is for calls, under its own retention.
